_clickable: every selector here is a control someone confirmed does NOT mutate — it navigates, filters, expands or dismisses. plan.py cannot check that (nothing in the markup says so), so this list IS the assertion. Adding one is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff. Never list a control that posts, votes, edits, withdraws, reports or deletes.

The 0.4.7 rect (x=4 y=0 w=1683 h=1040, chosen against a 1709x1255 capture) is retired, and so is its reasoning: it was measured when the one-page IA stacked all three boards for 2166 CSS px and the app overflowed its iframe. THE VIEWPORT OF RECORD MOVED: 1709x1255 → 1709x1711 (CSS 1498x1500 at the live DPR 1.140625, re-derived from the display, not copied). The WIDTH is unchanged on purpose — see `_widthIsNotFree`. The HEIGHT grew because the host sizes the iframe to the REMAINING VIEWPORT (`_iframeIsViewportCapped`) and the tallest board needs 1263 CSS px of iframe to render without scrolling. Probe: APPFRAME_RECT:104,64,-1,1709,1711,0; iframe CSS top 90.877, height 1352.178; capture PNG measured 1709x1711 with "via":"cdp". ── 🔴 THE VERTICAL SCROLLBAR IS GONE, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION. At the OLD viewport of record the app overflowed its iframe and a classic space-taking scrollbar ate the right edge (innerWidth 1498 vs documentElement.clientWidth 1483 = 15 CSS px), which is why the old rect stopped at w=1683. At 1498x1500 innerWidth == clientWidth == 1498 on ALL FIVE states (grids / matchups / prompts boards and both detail modals), so there is no scrollbar to clear. ⚠️ THE RISK THAT REPLACES IT: w=1700 puts the right edge at device 1704, only 5px from the frame's right edge, so IF the app ever overflows again the scrollbar lands inside the crop. That is not the failure to worry about — an overflow means the tallest state is clipped and the run is wrong anyway — but it is the tell to look for by eye. ── HORIZONTAL, IN CSS PX INSIDE THE APP FRAME, converted at ×1.140625: the ink is `app-layout`, x 24..1474 → device 27..1681. x=4 leaves a 23px left margin; w=1700 ends at 1704, a 23px right margin. SYMMETRIC BY CONSTRUCTION, which the old 4/1683 pair was not (23 left, 6 right — it was fighting the scrollbar). ── VERTICAL: y=0 is the iframe's own top edge and the app draws its header from its first pixel, so nothing is clipped above. h=1428 (frame-CSS 1252) is set by the PROMPTS BOARD, the tallest of the five states: its content ends at frame-CSS 1240 (`app-layout` y 99..1239, five `prompt-card`s at 817/903/990/1076/1163, each 77 tall), i.e. device 1414, and h=1428 clears it by 14px. The other four states end well above it — grids board frame-CSS 1068, matchups 1064, both detail modals 328 — so they carry 170-185 CSS px of flat app background below their content. 🔴 THAT DEAD BAND IS THE PRICE OF PHOTOGRAPHING ALL THREE BOARDS AND IT WAS A DELIBERATE CHOICE, not an oversight: see `_cropHeightTradeoff` for the alternative that was measured and rejected. ── 🔴 THE FLOATING SUPPORT WIDGET, RE-MEASURED AND ITS OFFSET DERIVED RATHER THAN COPIED. It is a TOP-FRAME element painted over the iframe: a span with background rgb(25,113,194), 42x36, inside an absolutely-positioned 92x48 container whose `bottom` is the page footer's height. Found with elementFromPoint, exactly as in the 0.4.7 note, so the widget itself has not changed. 🔴 WHAT IS NEW IS THAT ITS POSITION IS NOW EXPRESSED AS A CONSTANT: measured at TWO viewport heights (CSS 1440 → widget top 1347; CSS 1500 → widget top 1407), so widget top = innerHeight - 93 CSS, and with the iframe top pinned at CSS 91 the widget's top sits (innerHeight - 184) CSS BELOW THE IFRAME'S TOP EDGE — 1316 CSS = device 1501 at this viewport, i.e. absolute device y 1604. h=1428 ends at device 1532, so the clearance is 72px rather than the 0.4.7 rect's 5. ⚠️ THE TRAP THE OLD NOTE RECORDED STILL APPLIES IN ITS GENERAL FORM: a clearance argument is only valid for the rect it was made about. If h grows, re-derive this. `right: 70` does NOT save you — the exclusion bands apply to DETECTION and this is a declared rect. ── WHY full_frame DOES NOT FIRE: for a declared rect it is an AND on both axes against the PNG. w 1700/1709 = 99.5% (over 97%) but h 1428/1711 = 83.5% (under), so the AND is false. The height denominator is the CAPTURE, not the app frame — checked in `declared_box`, not assumed. ── 🔴 VERIFY BY EYE AFTER ANY RE-SHOOT: a declared rect makes the identical-box check INERT, and neither the bottom edge nor the support widget can be judged by any gate in this pipeline.

_cropHeightTradeoff: 🔴 THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL IN THIS RECIPE, RECORDED WITH THE NUMBERS THAT DECIDED IT, because `crop` has NO per-state override and one height has to serve five states whose content differs by 176 CSS px. Two candidates were measured against live 0.4.11: ── (a) h=1428 device (frame-CSS 1252) — SHIPPED. Every state complete, including all five `prompt-card`s of the prompts board. Cost: the grids and matchups assets carry ~170-185 CSS px of empty app background below their last card, and the crop aspect is 1700/1428 = 1.19 against the 1200x778 canvas's 1.542, so the render pillarboxes to 926x778 with a 137px pad on each side (~23% of the canvas). ── (b) h=1221 device (frame-CSS 1071) — REJECTED. It lands in the gutter between the prompts board's 3rd card (ends 1067) and its 4th (starts 1076), so every asset ends on a clean boundary, the grids and matchups assets have no dead band, and the aspect improves to 1.39 (≈1078x778 rendered, ~10% letterbox). Cost: the prompts asset shows 3 of 5 prompt cards. ── WHY (a) WON: the whole point of this pass is that the matchups and prompts boards became photographable again after the IA change made them unphotographable, and a prompts asset that stops two thirds of the way down is a weaker version of the thing being restored. The dead band is flat background of the same colour, which reads as margin; a truncated list reads as truncation. ⚠️ THIS IS A TASTE CALL AND IT IS REVERSIBLE IN ONE FIELD: if the listing wants the tighter frame, set `crop.rect.h` to 1221 and re-shoot — the viewport of record, the discriminators and the ledger are unaffected. Both numbers are live measurements; neither is carried over. ── ✅ AND THE LETTERBOX COST TURNED OUT TO BE ARITHMETIC ONLY, MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED ASSET RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `frame.py` pads the canvas with the SAME colour this app's background is: decoding `grids-board-framed.png` and scanning it, every pixel outside the content is rgb(26,27,30) and so is the app's own background — the ink occupies x 147..1052 of 1200 and the 137px pads either side are byte-identical to it, so there is no visible seam and no visible bar. That is why the 23% figure did not decide this and should not be quoted as if it were a visual defect. ⚠️ IT IS A PROPERTY OF THIS APP'S DARK THEME, NOT OF THE PIPELINE: re-check it if the app ever ships a lighter surface, because then the pad WOULD show.
_iframeIsViewportCapped: 🔴 THE MECHANISM IS UNCHANGED AND IT STILL DECIDES THIS RECIPE'S SHAPE — BUT THE CONCLUSION THE 0.4.7 NOTE DREW FROM IT IS NOW WRONG, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE OF THIS PASS. On the `/apps/run/<slug>` full-page surface the host does NOT fit the iframe to content: the iframe carries inline `flex: 1 1 0%` inside a flex parent with `overflow: hidden`, so it is sized to the REMAINING VIEWPORT HEIGHT and the app's overflow is clipped by the parent. Re-measured 2026-09-29 on 0.4.11 at three emulated CSS viewport heights — 1100 / 1440 / 1500 → iframe 952 / 1293 / 1352 CSS. The relationship is linear and constant: iframe height = innerHeight - 147 CSS, iframe top = CSS 91 at all three. ── 🔴 WHAT CHANGED: THE APP GOT SHORT ENOUGH THAT THE CAP STOPPED BINDING. The 0.4.7 note said `section-matchups` and `section-prompts` were 'UNPHOTOGRAPHABLE BY THIS PIPELINE' and that 'the store listing can no longer show a matchups view or a prompts view at all'. That was true of the one-page IA, which mounted all three boards at once for 2166 CSS px and put those two sections at y 1175..1482 and y 1500..2142 — below the iframe edge at every viewport tested. 0.4.11's `BoardNav` mounts ONE board at a time, and the app's own content height is now 1091 CSS (grids board) / 1089 (matchups) / 1263 (prompts), measured off `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` inside the app frame at the old viewport. The tallest of those, 1263, fits inside the iframe as soon as innerHeight ≥ 1263 + 147 = 1410 CSS. ✅ SO BOTH BOARDS ARE PHOTOGRAPHABLE AGAIN, AND THIS RECIPE PHOTOGRAPHS THEM: at the new viewport of record (CSS 1498x1500, iframe 1352) all three boards render with `documentElement.clientWidth == innerWidth == 1498` (no scrollbar) and `scrollY == 0` on every state. That closes the 'NOT MEASURED — a hypothesis for that follow-up, not a result' caveat the app repo left open in `src/components/BoardNav.tsx` and `src/capture-landmarks.test.tsx`; the answer is yes. ── ⚠️ AND A SECOND-ORDER MEASUREMENT WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE IT IS WHY THE VIEWPORT HAD TO GROW AT ALL: at the OLD viewport (CSS 1498x1100, iframe 952) clicking a board segment makes the browser scroll the segment into view — measured `scrollY` 137 on the matchups board and 139 on the prompts board, from 0. A capture taken there photographs a SCROLLED app: the open-grid panel is cut at the top and the prompts board is still clipped at the bottom. Making the iframe taller than the content removes the scroll entirely rather than depending on where a focus-scroll happens to land. ── 🔴 THERE IS STILL NO `scroll` VERB AND THIS NOTE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR ONE. `KNOWN_ACTIONS` in `plan.py` is click / clickIfPresent / type / key / waitForText / waitForGone / trustedKey / sleep / nav — re-read 2026-09-29, unchanged — and an unknown verb is REFUSED (`bad_recipe`), never skipped. The 0.4.7 note observed that a scroll verb now looks cheaper than once thought and warned the next reader not to read that as licence. The warning is kept, and it is now moot for this recipe: the boards are reached by making the frame taller, not by scrolling it.
_viewportOfRecord: 🔴 RE-RUNNING THIS RECIPE DOES NOT REQUIRE THE OPERATOR'S WINDOW TO BE THE ONE crop._measuredGeometry NAMES — EMULATE THE VIEWPORT INSTEAD. Measured 2026-09-08, re-confirmed 2026-09-27 (0.4.7) and re-derived 2026-09-29 for the NEW viewport of record against 0.4.11. 🔴 THE TRAP IS THAT TWO GATES READ DIFFERENT UNITS AND SATISFYING ONE BREAKS THE OTHER. `viewport_of_record` compares crop._measuredGeometry.viewport against the CAPTURE's pixel dimensions; `app_frame_scale` compares the PROBE's reading, which is CSS px × devicePixelRatio, against that same capture. `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` does NOT make window.devicePixelRatio return the overridden deviceScaleFactor — emulating the device figures at --dsf 1 satisfies `viewport_of_record` and then dies on `app_frame_scale`. ✅ THE SPELLING THAT WORKS: emulate in CSS px and let the scale factor carry the DPR, so both readings land on the same numbers — `browser --instance work --tab <id> emulate --width 1498 --height 1500 --dsf <live DPR>` (at the DPR measured today, 1.140625: 1498 × 1.140625 = 1708.7 → 1709; 1500 × 1.140625 = 1710.9 → 1711; the gates' tolerance is 2px). Confirmed end to end 2026-09-29: the probe answered APPFRAME_RECT:104,64,-1,1709,1711,0 and a raw CDP screenshot measured exactly 1709x1711. Then `capture.sh <recipe> --instance work --tab <id> --no-foreground`. 🔴 `--no-foreground` IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, NOT DIAGNOSTICS: an ACTIVE tab is captured by captureVisibleTab, which photographs real window pixels and IGNORES the emulation, so foregrounding silently re-introduces the mismatch. A tab opened by `browser open` is created inactive, which is what routes the capture onto CDP — and CDP honours the override. Confirm with `"via": "cdp"` in the screenshot op's answer. ⚠️ DERIVE --dsf FROM THE LIVE DISPLAY, DO NOT COPY 1.140625 — it is this operator's monitor today, not a constant; read devicePixelRatio and divide the recorded viewport by it. (2026-09-29: re-derived live from `window.devicePixelRatio`, still 1.140625 on a single 3440x1440 DP-0.) ⚠️ THE EMULATED HEIGHT IS NOT A FREE CHOICE ANY MORE and that is new for 0.4.11: it must leave the iframe taller than the tallest board or the app scrolls inside its own frame and a scrollbar returns — see `_iframeIsViewportCapped` for the 1263 CSS floor and the innerHeight-147 relationship. ⚠️ It also does NOT rescue the horizontal anchor: the live probe still answers leftInset=0 rightGap=-1, so this app IS still full-bleed and `xFrom`/`wFrom` remain ruled out for it — do not spend a session on that conversion. ✅ Evidence the y-anchor is earning its keep: appFrameTop moved 141 → 104 between the 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-08 readings and `yFrom: appFrame` absorbed it with no edit; it read 104 again on 2026-09-27 and again on 2026-09-29 at a viewport 456 device px taller.

🔴 THE MEASURED PRESENCE MATRIX — THIS IS THE CHECK, NOT THE PROSE ABOVE. `waitForText` is a SUBSTRING MATCH over the bridge `text` op's whole-frame output, and that output is DOM text.   string                                base  matchups-board  prompts-board  matchup-detail  prompt-detail
  'A grid is a named set of matchups'   YES   -               -              YES             YES            -> the GRIDS BOARD (3/5)
  'Submit and vote on checkpoint'       -     YES             -              -               -              -> UNIQUE
  'Submit and vote on prompts'          -     -               YES            -               -              -> UNIQUE
  'Matchup' + newline + U+00D7          -     -               -              YES             -              -> UNIQUE
  'Prompt'  + newline + U+00D7          -     -               -              -               YES            -> UNIQUE
  'Default (every ecosystem)'           -     -               -              -               YES            -> UNIQUE

and the strings this recipe used to carry, on the SAME five reads:
  'Build a grid'   absent in all five  (the Contribute menu is deleted)
  'Matchup'        PRESENT in all five (see the retraction below)
  'Top Grid'       PRESENT in all five
CONTROLS: 'ZZZ-absent-sentinel' returned absent in all five, and 'Model Benchmarking' returned present in all five — so the matcher can report both values and the zeros above are not a broken check. ── 🔴 THE RETRACTION, AND IT IS THE ONE THE 0.4.7 NOTE PREDICTED IN WRITING. That note flagged 'Matchup' as unique only BY CASE and said: 'if any future version renders a title-case Matchups heading anywhere on the page, this discriminator goes INERT SILENTLY'. 0.4.11's board subnav renders exactly that — the segment labels are the literals 'Grids' / 'Matchups' / 'Prompts' (`BOARDS` in `BoardNav.tsx`) — so 'Matchup' is a substring of the always-present 'Matchups' and is now PRESENT IN ALL FIVE READS. It is INERT and has been removed. The prediction was right, the guard was not self-correcting, and the only thing that caught it was re-running the matrix. RE-RUN IT; DO NOT TRUST IT. A discriminator that has stopped discriminating looks identical to one that works — five identical screenshots and exit 0. ── 🔴 THE WEAKEST LINKS NOW, FLAGGED ON PURPOSE. The two modal discriminators are the modal TITLE followed by its CLOSE GLYPH across an innerText line break — 'Matchup' + newline + U+00D7, and 'Prompt' + newline + U+00D7. The titles alone cannot work (they are substrings of the subnav's 'Matchups' / 'Prompts', the same trap in a new spelling), and the modal BODIES carry no static text at all: the third IA pass deleted every badge from `MatchupBody.tsx`, so everything inside the matchup modal is dataset ('Illustrious · v9.0', a LoRA name). The newline is real — measured in the live `text` output — but it is a claim about how innerText joins a title to a sibling button, which no test in either repo pins. `prompt-detail` has a second, sturdier anchor ('Default (every ecosystem)', a structural label from `PromptBody`) and this recipe asserts BOTH; `matchup-detail` has no equivalent and that asymmetry is real, not an omission. ── Why NOT a testid: `plan.py` emits `waitForText` as the `text` op with EMPTY argv, so the output is plain text with no attributes and a testid can never match. Selecting on the overlay's own `data-testid` would be the structurally better guard and the recipe form cannot express it. ── 🔴 THE NEEDLE IS MATCHED AGAINST THE BRIDGE'S RAW OUTPUT, NOT AGAINST THE DOM TEXT, AND THAT CHANGES HOW A NEWLINE MUST BE SPELLED. `capture.sh` does `case "$out" in *"$expect"*` where `$out` is the whole stdout+stderr of `browser --frame <f> text` — i.e. the bridge's JSON envelope, in which the page's newlines are already ESCAPED. Measured 2026-09-29 by reading the bytes: the raw output contains the two characters BACKSLASH and 'n' (not a newline) and the LITERAL 'U+00D7' character (not a \\u escape), so the two modal needles are written in this recipe as "Matchup\\n\u00d7" / "Prompt\\n\u00d7" — a JSON-escaped backslash followed by n. A needle containing a REAL newline cannot ever match. ✅ VERIFIED THROUGH THE REAL CODE PATH, not by reasoning about bash quoting: the plan's `expect` was extracted with capture.sh's own python one-liner (bytes `4d 61 74 63 68 75 70 5c 6e c3 97`) and fed to the same `case` statement — MATCH against the matchup-detail read, NO MATCH against the base read. Both controls in the same command. ⚠️ THE MATRIX ABOVE WAS ALSO RE-RUN AGAINST THE RAW OUTPUTS for this reason, not against the decoded text: an earlier pass of it used decoded text and would have shipped an unescaped needle that silently never matched. Every row above is a substring test on the exact bytes capture.sh sees.

That is the whole point of dating these: the count is a measurement, not a property. 🔴 The note that stood here until 2026-08-22 described a far thinner grid and ended by saying a well-framed capture of a nearly-empty app is still a nearly-empty app — true when written, and by now a standing veto on ever shooting this app. Read it as a MEASUREMENT with a date on it, not as a verdict. What has NOT changed: filling an empty cell SPENDS BUZZ, so it is deliberately not scripted here — the grid photographs whatever the crowd has already generated. ⚠️ DATASET CONTENT, STATED PLAINLY: the two detail states photograph a SPECIFIC matchup and a SPECIFIC prompt, because the recipe clicks the first row-group and the first column header, and the three board states photograph whatever rows the crowd has voted up. That is the one thing `shelf-life-and-what-not-to-shoot.md` says to avoid and it is unavoidable in this form — a board has to show SOMETHING. ⚠️ AND ONE ROW IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN: the grids board's only card is badged YOURS and carries a `Remove` button, which is account state in the frame. Weigh that before listing the grids asset; the matchups and prompts assets do not have it.

ready._comment: 🔴 RE-POINTED 2026-09-29, AND THE PREVIOUS GATE WAS NOT BROKEN — IT WAS BOARD-DEPENDENT. This was `section-grids`, which is correct only while the default board is `grids`: `BoardNav` mounts one board at a time and the unselected sections are ABSENT from the DOM, not hidden (asserted in the app repo's `src/boardNav.test.tsx`), so `section-grids` stops existing the moment a state clicks another segment. `results-grid` lives inside `section-open-grid`, which `App.tsx` renders on Home WHICHEVER board is selected, and it is the deepest landmark — it exists only once the open grid's matrix has resolved, which is the strictest 'the app has booted AND has data' signal this page offers. 🔴 THE GATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT `app-content` OR `app-surface`: both are the outer shell and would go true before the grid exists, which is the too-early gate this mechanism exists to prevent — a click fired into a still-booting app is discarded and the NEXT wait times out naming the wrong control. The recipe's own history records that misdiagnosis costing a session (the 0.4.7 `view-switch` gate arrived as a full 45s stall with no action attempted, which reads like a dead app). ── ✅ IT COVERS EVERY TRIGGER, BY STRUCTURE RATHER THAN CONTAINMENT. Two of the four triggers (`grid-group-matchup`, `grid-col-header`) are INSIDE `results-grid`. The other two (`board-nav-matchups`, `board-nav-prompts`) are not — but `BoardNav` is rendered in the same `view.kind === 'home'` branch as `section-open-grid` in `App.tsx`, so if `results-grid` resolved, `board-nav` is mounted. VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-29 rather than only read: after a `nav` to the app URL, a poll of the app frame every 2s from +2s to +12s found `results-grid`, `board-nav`, `section-open-grid`, `section-grids`, `grid-group-matchup` and `grid-col-header` present at EVERY sample, with `app-loading` absent at every sample (it had already resolved before the first read). `loadingTestid` is `app-loading`, which the served bundle carries (count 1); it was never observed true from here, so it is declared on the bundle's evidence and not on an observation of the loading state itself.

_howToDismissal: 🔴 THE FIRST ACTION OF EVERY STATE IS PROFILE-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS `clickIfPresent` AND NOT `click`. Dismissing the how-to PERSISTS across reloads (see `_noExplainerState`), so `[data-testid='howto-dismiss']` exists on a profile that has never run this app and is ABSENT on every profile that has. Re-measured 2026-09-29 on live 0.4.11: `howto-dismiss` is present in the served bundle (count 2) and the string 'How this works' is in the bundle (count 1) — but BOTH are absent from the live DOM and from all five whole-frame text reads on this operator's profile, so here the `clickIfPresent` skips and the `waitForGone` is satisfied instantly. Both are correct, and neither may be the only supported one: deleting the click breaks a fresh profile, while leaving it a plain `click` makes the bridge's `element_not_found` an action FAILURE on a used one. The `waitForGone` that follows is NOT dead and must stay: a wait-until-absent is satisfied instantly when the panel is already gone, and on a fresh profile it is the only thing stopping the next click from racing the dismissal. ⚠️ It is therefore VACUOUS on this profile — it proves nothing here, and that is not a reason to delete it.

_mutualExclusion: 🔴 EVERY STATE ASSERTS ITS OWN SURFACE IS OPEN *AND* THAT THE OTHERS ARE CLOSED, AND THE SECOND HALF IS NOT SYMMETRY FOR ITS OWN SAKE — IT IS A DEFECT THAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED INTO AN ASSET ON 2026-09-27 AND WAS CAUGHT BY EYE, NOT BY A GATE. THE INCIDENT: a full run exited 0, passed store-bounds, and produced an asset showing the Contribute dropdown AND a leftover Prompt detail panel open together. The single `waitForText` was satisfied — the string really was on screen — so nothing in the pipeline objected. ── THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: `capture.sh` reloads the app before every state EXCEPT THE FIRST ('the first state already landed'), so state 1 inherits whatever the tab was left in. Any run that passes `--tab <id>` of a tab someone has been clicking in is exposed; a tab `capture.sh` opens itself is not. ── ✅ ON 0.4.11 THE GUARD IS WIDER, BECAUSE THE STATE SET IS. Each board state now also asserts the OTHER TWO BOARDS are unmounted, which is a claim `BoardNav` makes cheap and exact: the unselected boards are ABSENT from the DOM, not hidden (the app repo asserts that by absence in `src/boardNav.test.tsx`, deliberately, because `display: none` would satisfy a visibility check while leaving every testid resolving). And each state asserts BOTH detail modals are closed. Measured 2026-09-29: opening one detail modal closes the other (`grid-group-matchup` then `grid-col-header` leaves exactly one), and a board click does not open either. ⚠️ THE 0.4.7 NOTE RECORDED THAT 'THEY ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE' HAD BEEN TOO NARROW A READING ONCE ALREADY — true of the pair tested, false of the pair not tested (the Contribute dropdown happily coexisted with a detail panel). That menu is gone, but the lesson is why every state asserts every other surface rather than the one it was observed to conflict with. ── WHY THE GUARD IS RIGHT RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND: it pins a RELATIONSHIP (this surface open, those closed) instead of a single word, so it fails LOUDLY — `waitForGone` polls until absent and then times out as an action failure (exit 4) naming the string — rather than silently photographing two surfaces. It does NOT repair a dirty tab and is not meant to; it converts a silent wrong-screen capture into a stopped run. ⚠️ IT IS VACUOUS ON A CLEAN RUN, which is exactly why it must not be deleted as dead weight. ── ✅ WATCHED FAILING AGAIN ON 2026-09-29, AND NOT ON PURPOSE, WHICH IS THE BEST KIND OF EVIDENCE. Immediately after the five-state run, a single-state re-run (`--state grids-board --tab <id>`) was fired at the SAME tab, which the previous run had left sitting on an open `prompt-detail` modal. `capture.sh` does not reload before the first state, so state 1 inherited it: the run reached step [8] and died on `TIMEOUT waiting for absence of Prompt\n\u00d7`, exit 4, NO ASSET SHIPPED. Without that `waitForGone` the run would have exited 0 and produced a grids-board asset with a prompt modal over it — which is exactly the 2026-09-27 incident, reproduced by accident two days later. The same run reloaded and re-run on a clean tab passed every step.
_statesRebuilt: 🔴 THE STATE SET CHANGED SHAPE AGAIN ON 2026-09-29, AND THIS TIME IT GREW. History, because each shape was forced by the app and not chosen: three TAB PANELS (matchups / prompts / grid) until 0.4.6; three OVERLAYS opened from the grid in 0.4.7, because the one-page IA put the matchups and prompts sections below the iframe's visible edge at every window size; and now FIVE STATES — three BOARDS plus the two detail modals. ── ✅ THE TWO NEW STATES ARE THE POINT OF THIS PASS. `matchups-board` and `prompts-board` restore views the store listing lost when the one-page IA shipped; `_iframeIsViewportCapped` carries the measurement that made them possible again and the heights that decided it. The Contribute state is GONE because the Contribute menu is gone, so the net change is +3 / -1. ── ⚠️ THE ASSETS' DIFFERENTIATION, HONESTLY. The three board states share the open-grid panel across their top 608 CSS px and differ below the subnav; the two detail states are the same page again with a small modal over it (matchup 582x224, prompt 582x182, both anchored at CSS y 104). So the FIVE are less different from each other than the OLD THREE tab panels were, and the two detail assets are the weakest of the set as standalone listing images. 🔴 A declared rect makes the identical-box check INERT, so nothing in the pipeline will tell you if any of these collapse into near-duplicates; that judgement is BY EYE and it is the reason this note exists. If the listing takes only three, take the three boards.
_noExplainerState: 🔴 There is deliberately NO `explainer` state, and it is not an oversight. Dismissing the how-to PERSISTS (it does not come back on reload), so the first state that dismisses [data-testid='howto-dismiss'] destroys it for every later state in the same run — the explainer state was tried last and captured nothing, because by then it was gone. Capturing it needs a profile that has never dismissed it, which this scripted path cannot arrange. custom-generators' recipe gets away with an `explainer` state only because it is listed FIRST. Do not 'fix' this by reordering: every state dismisses it as its first action, so whichever runs first still kills it.
